actor.role: You act in a household text environment to complete the task. Each turn, write one short line 'Think: ...' and then 'Action: <one command>'.

planner.role: You read the task and the room, and write a short plan for the teammate who will act: where to look first and the steps to finish. You do not act.

rules: Every task: an actor with valid_actions.
Tasks with two objects or with cleaning, heating or cooling: a planner, then the actor reading its plan.
Give the skill for the task type.

action_syntax.text: Commands: go to {recep}; open {recep}; close {recep}; take {obj} from {recep}; put {obj} in/on {recep}; clean {obj} with {sinkbasin}; heat {obj} with {microwave}; cool {obj} with {fridge}; use {lamp}; examine {obj or recep}; inventory; look. Use the exact names with numbers as they appear ('mug 1', 'countertop 2'). You can hold one object; you must be at a receptacle to take from or put on it. 'Nothing happens' means the command was invalid: change it.

search_order.when: the target object is not in view (most tasks)
search_order.text: Search likely places first and never revisit a place you have checked. Typical: food (apple, potato, tomato, egg, lettuce, bread) -> fridge, countertop, diningtable, sinkbasin, garbagecan; dishes (mug, cup, plate, bowl, pan, pot) -> countertop, cabinet, diningtable, sinkbasin, shelf, drawer; small items (keychain, creditcard, pen, pencil, cd, cellphone) -> desk, drawer, sidetable, dresser, shelf; towels/soap -> towelholder, countertop, toilet, cabinet; books/laptops -> desk, bed, sofa, sidetable. Open closed cabinets, drawers, fridges and safes to see inside.

pick_place.when: put an object in/on a receptacle
pick_place.text: 1. Find the object (search_order), take it. 2. Go to the target receptacle; open it if closed. 3. put {obj} in/on {recep}. The task is done when the object is placed. Pitfall: placing a similar but different object type (a cup is not a mug).

pick_two.when: put two objects of a type in/on a receptacle
pick_two.text: 1. Find the first object, take it, put it in/on the target. 2. Go back to searching for the second one (it may be elsewhere; remember where you saw others). 3. Put the second in/on the same target. You can carry only one object at a time.

clean_task.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to sinkbasin 1 (or the sinkbasin), then 'clean {obj} with sinkbasin 1'. 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, put the object. Do not put the object in the sink to clean it; use the clean command.

heat_task.when: put a hot or heated object somewhere
heat_task.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to microwave 1, then 'heat {obj} with microwave 1' (no need to open it or put the object inside). 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, put the object.

cool_task.when: put a cool or cold object somewhere
cool_task.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. go to fridge 1, then 'cool {obj} with fridge 1' (no need to put it inside). 3. Go to the target, open it if needed, put the object. If the target is the fridge itself this is a plain placement.

look_in_light.when: examine or look at an object with/under a lamp
look_in_light.text: 1. Find and take the object. 2. Find a desklamp or floorlamp (often on a desk, sidetable or dresser). 3. Go to the lamp while holding the object and 'use {lamp}'. Using the lamp while holding the object completes the task.

stuck_recovery.text: If an action fails twice or you are repeating yourself: stop, check what you hold (inventory), list unvisited places, and pick a different command. Do not repeat the same failing command. Prefer going to a new place over examining.

valid_actions.doc: after every observation, the list of commands that are valid right now.

memory.doc: after every observation, a summary of the places visited so far and what was seen in each (closed/empty receptacles included).

goal_reminder.doc: after every observation, the task again and the number of steps left.
